messages.author: a5d94cca01490293
messages.subject: Monotonically decreasing function
parts:
Hi,

I have a problem with my data. If I use this function (cmod11 <- mirt(rev, 1, itemtype='Rasch')) I will have monotonically increasing functions for all items, but if I use itemtype='2PL' or '3PL', I will have monotonically decreasing functions for some items (see images). Why does this happen? Thanks a lot.

Danilo
Brazil

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Monotonically decreasing function
parts:
Hi Danilo,

It depends on the nature of the items, which we don't know. You'd have to look at why these have negative or not slopes (are they reverse scored, measure a distinct factor, have dramatically different content compared to other items, etc). In any case, definitely do not use a Rasch model since that is very very bad. The Rasch model fixes all the slopes to be equal by definition, so it will fit these data incredible poorly (stats like M2() and itemfit() will make this apparent, but you'll also see a massive drop in things like BIC/AIC and the log-likelihoods).  

Regarding the 3PL model, unless you have a huge amount of data (2000+ individuals) you'll need to include normal priors on the lower bound parameters to keep them stable. It's a common problem with that model, and freely estimating the g parameters is generally not recommended. Cheers.

Phil

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Monotonically decreasing function
parts:
Hi Sue,

See the first few examples in the ?mirt help file, there is a portion showing how to set up a logit prior for the g parameters. Freely estimating the g parameter can cause wild and uncontrollable issues, including local minimum and non-convergence. This tends to go away in larger sample sizes, but due to the nature of the model the g terms cause a lot of additional problems (much harder to estimate standard errors/posterior deviations because the likelihood is much flatter). Cheers. 

Phil

Phil

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Monotonically decreasing function
parts:
The guessing parameters are stored as logits, and -1.5 was just my selected location as an example. If, for instance, you wanted the g values to be centered around .2, then you would need to change -1.5 to log(.2/(1-.2)) = -1.386. The 3 is the variance of this prior, where a smaller value means a stronger prior (larger values make it more diffuse). Justifying how tight this prior should be is a matter of personal or prior information collected from previous literature; such is the issue with all Bayesian applications, and here it's no different. 

And yes, 5 is referring to the 5th item. See ?mirt.model for more information on how to specify additional items.

Phil
